# Best power station + solar combos for an RV

The only direct purchase links in my search results come from Dealectric, which earns a commission on purchases through its links at no cost to you. The tested codes there are for Bluetti and ALLPOWERS, so those are the kits I can link.

## My picks

**1. Best all-rounder: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar kit**
- 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W
- $1,199, or $1,139.05 with code AFF5OFF
- It has enough capacity for a fridge, lights, laptops and Starlink for a day or two.
- [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit) (source 1)

**2. Most solar for the money: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit**
- 1,451 Wh, 2,400 W, with a 400 W foldable panel
- $963, or $866.70 with code ALLPOWERS26
- The 400 W panel recharges noticeably faster than the 200 W panels in the Bluetti kits.
- [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit) (source 1)

**3. Budget or weekend trips: BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W solar kit**
- 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W
- $769, or $730.55 with code AFF5OFF
- [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit) (source 1)

## If you want to run a roof air conditioner
The kits above likely won't do it. A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup (source 6). You'd need a bigger station, such as the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,000 W, 4,096 Wh) or Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,000 W, 3,024 Wh). Both are described in [this RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), but my results didn't include a direct purchase link for either.

The **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) has a built-in 30A RV outlet (source 6) and a high solar input ceiling of 1,200 W (source 7). It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, but it's sold without a panel, so you'd add panels separately. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

## Tips
- **Check the solar input limit.** A power station caps how much solar it accepts, so a big panel array can be wasted on a unit with a low ceiling (source 5). The Bluetti AC200L is high at 1,200 W. Confirm the limit for any model you buy.
- **Size by your loads.** Add up watts × hours. A 150 W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500 Wh (source 2).
- **Chemistry.** Current models from these brands use LiFePO4, which lasts thousands of cycles (sources 4, 5).
- **Codes.** They were tested in the brand carts on Oct 25, 2025 listings, and the store's checkout has the final word. Prices can change.

If you tell me what you plan to run (roof AC, fridge, Starlink, CPAP) and how many nights you'll be off-grid, I can narrow this to one pick.
